projects.name: OpsPilot
projects.summary: An agentic RAG copilot for on-call incident response. Given an alert, it searches runbooks and past postmortems, checks deploys, metrics, and logs through tool calls, and returns a diagnosis that cites its evidence.
projects.outcome: Hybrid search (BM25 + dense vectors, fused with RRF) reached 1.000 hit@5 and 1.000 MRR on a golden dataset, versus 0.909 MRR for either method alone, enforced by a CI gate. A deterministic verifier drops made-up citations, logs are screened for prompt injection, and actions that change production need human approval.

case_study.problem: When a production alarm fires, on-call engineers often spend the first 15 to 30 minutes just connecting it to a recent deploy, a moving metric, and the right runbook. The knowledge exists, but it's scattered across docs, dashboards, and logs.
case_study.approach: An agent that works like a careful on-call engineer: it retrieves relevant runbooks and past postmortems, investigates live signals with read-only tools, writes a structured diagnosis, and has that diagnosis checked by code before anyone sees it.

diagram.detail: Deploys, metrics, logs via tool calls
Citations and confidence checked in code

decisions.title: Hybrid search instead of embeddings alone
decisions.detail: Incident text is full of exact identifiers like v2.14.0 and max.poll.interval.ms that embeddings blur. BM25 keyword search catches those, dense search catches paraphrases, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines them by rank with no score tuning.

decisions.title: Code checks the model's citations
decisions.detail: Everything the agent sees gets an evidence ID. A deterministic verifier drops citations that don't exist, caps confidence when an answer isn't backed by live telemetry, and escalates to a human when unsure.

decisions.title: Logs are treated as untrusted input
decisions.detail: Log lines can contain text written by attackers. OpsPilot flags prompt-injection attempts, redacts secrets and card numbers before the model sees them, and never runs an action that changes production without human approval.

decisions.title: A state machine instead of an agent framework
decisions.detail: Explicit steps with hard budgets on steps, tool calls, and tokens make every path unit-testable and put an upper bound on cost and latency.

case_study.result: 1.000 hit@5 and 1.000 MRR on a golden dataset with hybrid search, versus 0.909 MRR for either method alone, enforced as a CI quality gate. 65+ automated tests cover the agent, guardrails, and retrieval, and the AWS infrastructure is defined as code with CDK.

projects.tagline: An AI copilot that diagnoses production alerts and cites its evidence.

projects.name: DealRadar
projects.summary: A full-stack price tracker for Amazon products: paste a product link, and it scrapes the price, charts its history, and flags a deal when the price drops below your target.
projects.outcome: Flask and MySQL backend where database triggers and stored procedures detect price drops, a scraper that handles deals, price ranges, and hidden prices, Chart.js price-history charts, and deal news pulled from RSS feeds.

case_study.problem: Online prices change constantly, and good deals disappear before anyone notices. Checking products by hand doesn't scale past a few items.
case_study.approach: Paste an Amazon product link. A scraper collects the price, the database records every change, and a dashboard charts price history and flags a deal when the price drops below your target.

decisions.title: Deal detection lives in the database
decisions.detail: MySQL triggers and stored procedures compare each new price with the user's target, so the alert logic runs exactly where the data changes.

decisions.title: A scraper built for messy product pages
decisions.detail: It handles deal prices, price ranges, and hidden prices instead of assuming every page shows one clean number.

decisions.title: Context beyond the price
decisions.detail: Deal news from RSS feeds sits next to the price-history charts, so users see why a price might be moving.

case_study.result: A working full-stack app: Flask backend, a MySQL schema with triggers and stored procedures, a resilient scraper, and an interactive price-history dashboard.

projects.tagline: A price tracker that charts Amazon price history and flags deals.
